SeriesStatAccessor API Reference¶

Back to Series API Reference

SeriesStatAccessor groups statistical reductions, normal-distribution functions, trailing-window calculations, normalization transforms, and pairwise distances. Start here when the question is statistical rather than a generic elementwise or shape operation.

Calling Styles¶

Unary methods have two equivalent spellings:

auto a = x.stat.mean(0);
auto b = x.stat().mean(0);

The first calls the accessor directly. The second creates a SeriesStatProxy bound to x, then calls the same implementation. Prefer direct style for ordinary code; recognize proxy style because it becomes useful for binary methods:

auto direct = left.stat.cdist(right);
auto bound = left.stat(right).cdist();

Here stat(right) binds the peer before the terminal method is selected. The owner left remains the first point table in either spelling.

Describing A Population¶

  • mean summarizes location globally or by axis.

  • var measures squared spread with sample or population normalization.

  • std reports the same spread in original units.

  • nanvar and nanstd omit NaNs under an explicit missing-observation policy.

  • skewness measures asymmetry.

  • kurtosis reports excess fourth-moment shape.

Axis choice defines the population being summarized. On a matrix, dim=0 groups values by column and dim=1 groups them by row. A global statistic pools all entries and generally cannot be reconstructed by averaging lane-wise statistics.

Evaluating A Normal Model¶

  • pdf gives local density.

  • logpdf gives log density.

  • cdf gives accumulated lower-tail probability.

  • logcdf preserves very small lower-tail values in log space.

All four preserve shape and support standard normal, scale-only, and explicit (mu,sigma) overloads. These methods evaluate a chosen normal model; they do not estimate mu or sigma from the owner.

Following A Trailing Window¶

  • movsum and movmean track local level.

  • movmin and movmax track local bounds.

  • movvar and movstd track local population spread.

Every moving method preserves shape, includes the current position, looks backward, and uses the available prefix before a full window exists. Omitted arguments mean window three on the last axis.

Transforming Statistical Geometry¶

  • center subtracts a global or lane mean.

  • standardize produces population z-scores.

  • normr gives nonzero rows unit L2 length.

  • normc gives nonzero columns unit L2 length.

These operations all preserve shape, but they solve different problems. Centering removes offset, standardization removes offset and spread, and norm operations remove vector magnitude without subtracting a mean.

Comparing Point Tables¶

  • cdist computes all Euclidean row-to-row distances between two rank-2 point tables.

  • pdist2 provides the equivalent two-table pairwise-distance surface; the 2 does not mean squared distance.

For owner shape [m,d] and peer shape [n,d], both return [m,n] and differentiate with respect to both point tables.
